summary: An email-first publication by one writer or a small desk: the subscribe form is the hero, the latest letter proves the voice, a searchable archive and single-issue pages do the rest.

pages.purpose: Turn a visitor into a subscriber: what it is, how often, a real sample, who writes it and what readers say.

sections.purpose: A newspaper-style nameplate with the promise, the subscribe form and the reader count, beside the latest letter.
alternatives: form-01: a custom form when readers also choose a cadence (every letter / monthly digest)
fields: Latest letter: number, date, title, first paragraph
sections.notes: Email field with a typo hint for common domains linked to the input (aria-describedby); after submit show the double opt-in step in a role="status" region with the address to check and an undo. The latest letter shows its opening with a drop cap and a 'continue reading' link.

sections.purpose: The last few letters as ruled rows, with a topic index beside them.
alternatives: blog-list: card list when letters have cover images
fields: Per letter: number, title, dek, topic, date, reading time
sections.notes: Each topic opens the archive pre-filtered.

sections.purpose: Who writes it and why, beside a photo.

fields: Reader quotes with name or role and permission

sections.purpose: Cost, cadence, unsubscribing, replying to letters, data use.

pages.purpose: Every letter, searchable in full text, filterable by topic and year, with the subscribe form at hand.

sections.purpose: How many letters and since when.
Full-text search across titles, deks and body; topic and year switches; results by year with matches highlighted.
alternatives: empty-state: when nothing matches, offering to drop the filters
sections.notes: Diacritics-insensitive matching in every language the site uses; '/' can focus the search box (documented, ignored while typing); live result count in a polite region; a 'clear filters' action.

sections.purpose: The subscribe card beside the results.

pages.purpose: One letter as it arrives in the inbox, then a reason to subscribe and the neighbouring letters.

sections.purpose: Issue number in the margin, date, reading time, topic, the body with a drop cap and a pulled sentence, and the sign-off.
Subscribe card at the end of the letter.
alternatives: cta: a plain band linking to the home form

content: Cadence and delivery day; free or paid
Back issues: number, title, dek, topic, date, full text
FAQ answers: cost, unsubscribing, replying, data use
Email service that does double opt-in, and the sender address

styles.name: slow desk
styles.why: Old-style book serif headlines over a screen serif, mono datelines, a double rule under the nameplate and an ink-red accent; postmark and drop cap details. Suits a personal essay or culture newsletter.

styles.name: briefing
styles.why: Compact grotesk and clear lists; for a weekly industry or market briefing.

pitfalls: Signup without double opt-in, explicit consent or a privacy link; say what is sent and how often next to the button.
Inflated or stale subscriber counts; show a count only if it is true and kept current.
Subscribe success that is not announced to screen readers, or a typo hint not linked to the email field.
An archive search that misses words written with or without diacritics.
Letters only available in the inbox: every issue should have its own page and stay linkable.
Reader quotes used without permission or attributed to full names that readers did not agree to show.
